# Narrowed goal: what the budget work still needs

Most of this plan shipped as four smaller pull requests rather than the
eight-phase train it was drafted as. What follows is only the part that did not,
restated against the tree as it now stands. Nothing below assumes the bucket
budget design: that design was replaced by a ratio, which needs no config format,
no migration, and no new CLI flags.

## Already shipped, do not re-plan

- **P1** — one fence-masked `headingSpans` in `scripts/plan-lint.mjs`; `headingsOf`
  and `planHalves` both read it. It also fixed a live defect: a plan showing a
  template heading inside a code fence satisfied the template check without
  having the section at all.
- **E** — a lint-gated round is measured against the last lint-gated round, never
  against a reviewed count, and the outcome carries `gatingIssueKind` so the next
  pass seeds the scoreboard the count came from.
- **I**, **A**, **H** — superseded. The specification/record split ships as a
  ratio: a record half past a third of the two halves is a major finding in
  `lintPlanDocument`, so it gates a round rather than waiting for a train. The cut
  is calibrated on the four-plan corpus, which separates 24.4% (shipped) from
  46.1/45.6/47.4% (abandoned). No buckets, so **P2** is moot entirely.
- **J** — the drafting and review prompts state the two halves and the
  under-a-third bar directly.
- **B** — the record-share finding names each record section by size, largest first, and
  offers the plan’s largest code block as a compression candidate.
- **L** — the ceiling finding no longer asserts a cause it cannot see, and points
  at the record-share finding, which can.
- Shipped alongside: `altitudeIssues` recalibrated from 100% of estimated code to
  75%, which it could not previously reach; and `planMovement`, which reports a
  pass that handed back the plan it was given.

## What remains

**F (partial). Per-revision growth.** `planMovement` measures one pass end to end.
It does not measure a revision against the critiques that revision was asked to
resolve, which is the narrower signal: a revision that grew the plan while
resolving nothing. Worth doing only if a real run shows the per-pass number is too
coarse.

**C. Near-duplicate paragraph detection.** Dropped, and the reason it was parked
was wrong. That reason said a non-gating lint finding reaches nobody; it does —
every one comes back as `advisoryIssues` and `commands/plan.md` shows them after
the plan and before the approval question. That premise was true when this plan
was drafted and the plumbing has since been built, which is a fair warning about
every other premise in this file.

The half of C that was certain — the plan's largest code block, by length and
line — now rides inside the record-share finding, where it is only ever offered
beside a finding that already fired. What is dropped is near-duplicate paragraph
detection: with per-section attribution naming the large section outright,
guessing at duplicates adds noise rather than information, and the false
positives this plan already listed are real ones.

**K. An accepted-overrun path.** A human-accepted gating finding. Unchanged from
the original assessment: net-new surface with no local precedent, needing a
schema-bound override artifact, an acceptance scope, an owner, resume and approval
verification, and invalidation rules. Still the largest item here, and less
obviously wanted than it was — the ratio check makes the common overrun
diagnosable, which was most of the motivation for an override.

## Hard constraints

Unchanged: the subtractive-revision rule, the fixed template, the divergence
detector, and `largePlanWarningChars`. Compaction never runs after a clean round.
